Landing page optimization guide: 20 Proven tips, examples & best practices
==========================================================================

Dragos Voicila Content marketing manager

22 July 2025

Learn proven landing page optimization strategies to boost conversions, reduce bounce rates, and maximize ROI for your marketing campaigns.

**

Landing pages serve as the decisive moment in your marketing funnel, converting visitor intent into concrete actions like sign-ups, purchases, or inquiries. Through effective landing page optimization, you can achieve a higher click-through rate (CTR), better-quality leads, and stronger conversion rates without extra ad spend.  
  

But accomplishing all that takes more than attractive design. It needs deliberate structure, messaging, and testing.  
  

This guide covers **everything you need to know about landing page optimization**:

**

*   Clear definitions and key differences from other web pages

**

*   20 proven tips, backed by examples and best practices  
    
*   How Edicy simplifies landing page optimization
    

Read on if you’re looking for a straightforward blueprint to boost conversions.

What is the meaning of landing page optimization?
-------------------------------------------------

  

Landing page optimization is the art of turning casual clicks into committed actions, one tweak at a time. How? By enhancing various elements to make every click count, instead of simply gaining more traffic.  
  

By strategically fine-tuning headlines, visuals, and calls to action (CTAs), you shepherd prospects through each step of their decision journey, from the moment they arrive on your page to the instant they hit “submit.” Optimizing layout, loading speed, and trust signals minimizes hesitation and builds confidence, so visitors engage further. In doing so, you transform every interaction into a meaningful nudge toward your goal.  
  

So, whatever your goal — leads, conversions, or sales — optimization pushes it further. When every pixel pulls its weight, your page goes from performing to converting.

### Landing page optimization vs. website optimization

  

Here's how landing page optimization differs from website optimization.  
  


**

**Landing page optimization** revolves around one goal (like sign-ups or sales), making every element serve that single purpose. It’s campaign-specific, distraction-free, and built to convert fast. **Website optimization** supports a wider range of goals, from brand storytelling to SEO and user navigation. It’s about improving the full experience across multiple pages and audiences.

**

In terms of metrics, **landing page optimization** focuses on conversion rate, while website optimization leans on bounce rate, time on site, and page views. Each tells a different story about performance and intent.

****  

Landing page visitors are primed to act, so [**landing page design**](https://www.edicy.com/blog/landing-page-design-for-higher-conversions)
 **optimization**

****

should guide, not distract. **Website optimization** should better help users explore, compare, and learn, requiring intuitive navigation and layered content.

****  

💡 In other words, landing pages drive immediate action while websites build long-term trust and discovery. Optimizing each for its role means better results across the entire [customer journey](https://www.textmagic.com/blog/b2b-customer-journey-map/)
.  

  ![Differences between landing page optimization and websit optimization](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Differences%20between%20landing%20page%20optimization%20and%20website%20optimization_block.webp "Differences between landing page optimization and websit optimization")

20 actionable landing page optimization tips
--------------------------------------------

  

Want more conversions from your landing pages? These 20 actionable tips will help you boost performance, reduce bounce rates, and turn more clicks into customers.

### How to optimize a landing page for lead generation

  

Your landing page should make it ridiculously easy for visitors to say “yes.” These tips help you capture high-quality leads without friction.

#### 1\. Use clear, compelling headlines that instantly show what’s in it for them

  

People scan before they read. If your headline doesn’t hook them in under 5 seconds, they’re gone.  
  

Therefore, lead with the payoff. For example, “Get 3x More Bookings Without Doubling Ad Spend.” Use direct language that reflects your ad or offer.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t use headlines like “Welcome” or “Let’s Get Started.” Those say nothing and sell nothing.

  


****

#### 2\. Keep forms short and ridiculously easy to complete

  ![Keeping forms short as a landing page optimization technique](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Screenshot%202025-07-22%20at%2013.18.06%201_block.webp "Keeping forms short as a landing page optimization technique")

Every extra field is a reason to bounce. Users aren’t here for paperwork; they’re here for value.

  

So, stick to the essentials: name + email. Want more info? Use progressive profiling or multi-step forms.

  

👍**Pro tip:** Label your submit button with the benefit, not the action. For example, “Get the Free Guide” > “Submit.”

  


****

#### 3\. Offer a strong lead magnet they’d actually trade their email for

  ![Offering a strong lead magnet as a landing page optimization technique](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/salesforce%2027_block.webp "Offering a strong lead magnet as a landing page optimization technique")

Image source: [salesforce.com](https://www.salesforce.com/eu/form/newsletter/?d=pb)

  

People don’t hand over personal info without a clear win. You need to give before you ask.  
  

Offer something bite-sized and instantly useful, like a checklist, a cheat sheet, or a free audit. Bonus if it solves a nagging problem.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t call it a “newsletter.” Nobody wakes up excited to subscribe to more emails.

  


****#### 4\. Use social proof to silence hesitation and build instant trust

  ![Using social proof as a landing page optimization technique](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Screenshot%202025-07-22%20at%2013.19.37%201_block.webp "Using social proof as a landing page optimization technique")**  

Image source: [textmagic.com](https://www.textmagic.com/)

[](https://www.salesforce.com/eu/form/newsletter/?d=pb)
**

We look to others before we act, especially online. Validation reduces risk.

If possible, add a client logo bar, a brief testimonial, or a user count (“Trusted by 12,000+ marketers”) near your CTA.  
  

👍 **Pro tip:** Use faces when you can. Testimonials with photos increase trust dramatically.

  


****

#### 5\. Design like a minimalist with a conversion goal

  

Visual clutter leads to cognitive overload and decision paralysis. A clean design guides action.  
  

Think of it this way: one column, one CTA, ample white space. Remove anything that doesn’t move users closer to your goal.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t bury your CTA in a sea of competing elements. If it’s hard to find, it won’t get clicked.

  


****

### Landing page SEO optimization tips

  

Search engines can bring you qualified traffic for free, but only if you play by their rules and keep users happy. Here’s how to optimize for both robots and real people.

#### 6\. Use a keyword-rich H1 that tells both Google and visitors what you’re about

  

Your H1 is prime real estate. It signals relevance to search engines and sets expectations for readers.  
  

Drop your primary keyword into a benefits-focused headline. For example, “Get Affordable Team Messaging with Text Automation.”  
  

👍 **Pro tip:** Don’t force it. If the keyword makes the headline awkward, Google (and humans) will notice.

  


****

#### 7\. Add title tags and meta descriptions that act like your ad in search results

  ![Adding title tags and meta descriptions as landing page optimization techniques](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Screenshot%202025-07-21%20at%2014.40.26%20copy_large.webp "Adding title tags and meta descriptions as landing page optimization techniques")

Your meta title is the headline of your search result, so you’d better make it count. Treat it like your 160-character elevator pitch.  
  

Keep title tags under 60 characters, and make sure your meta description includes a hook and a CTA. Think: “Automate your texts. Boost response rates. Start free.”  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t stuff keywords or write like a bot. Write like someone whose work is worth clicking on.

  


****

#### 8\. Use alt text for images to boost crawlability

  ![Using alt text as a landing page optimization technique](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Screenshot%202025-07-21%20at%2014.42.27%20copy_block.webp "Using alt text as a landing page optimization technique")

Search engines can’t see images, but they can read descriptions. And users with screen readers rely on them.  
  

So, describe what the image shows in clear, specific terms. For example, “Dashboard showing SMS campaign metrics” > “Chart.”  
  

👍 **Pro tip:** Use your keyword where relevant, but only if it makes sense in context.

  


****

#### 9\. Optimize for lightning-fast load times

  

Google prioritizes pages that load fast. Your users do too, especially if they’re on the go.  
  

Use tools like PageSpeed Insights. Compress images, ditch heavy scripts, and make sure your layout doesn’t break on small screens.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t rely on desktop previews. Test it on your phone, then test it again.

  


****

#### 10\. Add internal links (sparingly) to support your site’s SEO structure

  

Internal links help Google crawl your site and help users keep exploring.  
  

So, use descriptive anchor text to link to relevant resources like blog posts or pricing pages. For example: “See our pricing breakdown” > “Click here.”  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t overdo it. Too many links can feel spammy and kill your conversion focus.

  


****

### Design & UX tips for higher engagement

  

Every design choice is a cue for user behavior. These tips help you create landing pages that feel intuitive, load fast, and keep people scrolling (and converting).  

#### 11\. Use visual hierarchy and whitespace to guide the eye like a pro

  ![Using whitespace as a landing page optimization technique](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/19.%20Voog_block.webp "Using whitespace as a landing page optimization technique")

If your message isn’t skimmable, it’s skippable. A good hierarchy tells them where to look next without thinking.  
  

Make headlines bigger, CTAs bolder, and supporting copy lighter. Leave breathing room between sections so the page doesn’t feel like a wall of noise.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t cram everything above the fold. Let your content breathe. Scroll is free real estate.

  


****

#### 12\. Make sure your design is fully responsive, because desktop is not the default

  

More than [60%](https://whatsthebigdata.com/mobile-internet-traffic/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
 of traffic is mobile. If your layout breaks on a phone, your conversions will too.  
  

Use flexible grids, large tappable buttons, and font sizes that scale. Preview on multiple devices before launch.  
  

👍 **Pro tip:** Test thumb zones. If users have to pinch and zoom, you’ve already lost them.

  


****

#### 13\. Use high-contrast CTA buttons that beg to be clicked

  ![Using high-contrast CTAs as a landing page optimization technique](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/5.%20Mailchimp_block.webp "Using high-contrast CTAs as a landing page optimization technique")

Image source: [mailchimp.com](https://mailchimp.com/landers/email-marketing-platform/?ds_c=DEPT_AOC_Google_Search_ROW_EN_Brand_Acquire_Omega_Manual-NE_T3&ds_kids=p81005570474&ds_a_lid=kwd-2285511033&ds_cid=71700000120288589&ds_agid=58700008803527157&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=21865451006&gbraid=0AAAAADh1Fp3rRfLiP6ygRh8C0w8G4A13A&gclid=CjwKCAjw24vBBhABEiwANFG7y7OX8nLtcHrgBKFPnlc0MJiaSi5qOZrzcoxWpG_mtwLkPAk_XDQL7RoCKRYQAvD_BwE&gclsrc=aw.ds&currency=EUR)

[](https://mailchimp.com/landers/email-marketing-platform/?ds_c=DEPT_AOC_Google_Search_ROW_EN_Brand_Acquire_Omega_Manual-NE_T3&ds_kids=p81005570474&ds_a_lid=kwd-2285511033&ds_cid=71700000120288589&ds_agid=58700008803527157&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=21865451006&gbraid=0AAAAADh1Fp3rRfLiP6ygRh8C0w8G4A13A&gclid=CjwKCAjw24vBBhABEiwANFG7y7OX8nLtcHrgBKFPnlc0MJiaSi5qOZrzcoxWpG_mtwLkPAk_XDQL7RoCKRYQAvD_BwE&gclsrc=aw.ds&currency=EUR)
  

CTAs should be obvious. If visitors have to hunt for them, they won’t bother.  
  

Therefore, choose a button color that pops against your background. Think blue on white, orange on navy, not subtle greys.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t bury your CTA in a sea of text, nor match it to your background. You’re hunting conversions, not chameleons.

  


****

#### 14\. Add explainer videos or subtle animations to clarify, not distract

  

Viewers retain [95%](https://speach.me/blog/7-stats-that-prove-why-video-instructions-are-more-effective-than-written?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
 of a video's message compared to 10% when reading text. That is, if it’s used with purpose.  
  

Use short (<60 sec) videos to walk users through a process or show off product features. Keep animations smooth and sparing, with no flashing banners or spinning logos.  
  

👍 **Pro tip:** Always include captions. Many users watch on mute.

  


****#### 15\. Use scroll behavior analytics to find (and fix) dead zones

  ![Using heatmaps as a landing page optimization technique](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Hotjar-711x1024.png "Using heatmaps as a landing page optimization technique")**  

Image source: [textmagic.com](https://www.textmagic.com/blog/customer-engagement-metrics/)

**

You can’t optimize what you can’t see. Scroll maps reveal where users lose interest.  
  

Tools like Hotjar or Clarity show where visitors stop reading, rage-click, or scroll past your CTA. Adjust the layout accordingly.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t assume everyone reads top to bottom. Some of your best content might be invisible without data.

  


****

### How to improve landing page conversion rate

  

Getting clicks only means you’re visible. Our goal is to get you from “visible” to “valuable”, and that translates into conversions. The following tips help turn “maybe later” into “take my money.”

#### 16\. Run A/B tests like your ROI depends on it — because it does

  ![Running A/B tests as a landing page optimization technique](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/CTA_block.webp "Running A/B tests as a landing page optimization technique")

What you like doesn’t matter. What converts does.  
  

Start with big-impact variables: headline, CTA, offer. Test one element at a time and give it enough traffic to reach statistical confidence.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t call a test too early. Let the data breathe before making changes.

  


****#### 17\. Write CTA buttons that punch above their weight

  ![Writing punchy CTAs as a landing page optimization technique](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/7.%20Jolie_block.webp "Writing punchy CTAs as a landing page optimization technique")**  

Image source: [jolieskinco.com](https://jolieskinco.com/pages/water-report)

**

“Submit” is a shrug. A strong CTA makes the action irresistible.  
  

Use first-person, action-focused phrases tied to value. For example, “Start My Free Trial,” “Send Me the Tips,” “Book My Demo.”  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Avoid vague or passive language like “Learn More” or “Click Here”. Those say nothing and convert even less.

  


****

#### 18\. Strip out distractions like nav bars, footers, and links to nowhere

  

Every extra option is a chance to not convert. Fewer exits = more completions.  
  

Use a clean, single-purpose layout. Ditch global nav, sidebars, and any links that don’t push toward your goal.  
  

👍 **Pro tip:**  If you're worried about SEO or user needs, add collapsible sections or microcopy. Just don’t overload the page visually.

  


****

#### 19\. Mirror your ad copy to keep the message consistent from click to CTA

  

If the landing page doesn’t reflect the ad they clicked, visitors get disoriented. Or worse, annoyed.  
  

Reuse key phrases, offers, and tone from your ad in the headline and hero section. Maintain the emotional thread.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t promise a free guide in the ad and deliver a demo form. That’s a bait-and-bounce move.

  


****

#### 20\. Add urgency that’s honest, not gimmicky

  

Deadlines move people. Without one, “later” becomes “never.”  
  

Use countdown timers, such as “Only X Spots Left,” or phrases like “Offer Ends Sunday.” But make sure the timer is real.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t overdo it. Scarcity works best when it’s grounded in truth. If everything’s “limited-time,” nothing is.

****Three real-world landing page optimization examples
---------------------------------------------------

  

Want to see what great landing page optimization looks like in action? Here are three real-world examples that turned clicks into conversions.

### Flare: Trust signals elevated = increased credibility & scroll retention

  ![Flare landing page before & after optimization](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Flare_block.webp "Flare landing page before & after optimization")

Image sources: [web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20240610083653/https://try.flare.io/book-a-demo/)
; [try.flare.io](https://try.flare.io/book-a-demo/)

#### What changed

*   Strong offer in 2024 (“14-day full access”), but the absence of any trust cues above the fold made the value proposition feel unanchored
    
*   In the 2025 version, Flare introduces a “Verizon Business Contributor” badge right under the offer
    

#### Impact

*   A high-trust brand marker (e.g., Verizon) near the headline instantly boosts perceived legitimacy, especially among enterprise or compliance-driven decision-makers
    
*   It also visually breaks up the hero without clutter
    

#### What you can learn

*   A well-placed trust badge can outperform paragraphs of copy
    
*   Use recognizable brand associations above the fold to build instant authority
    

### Slite: Reworked visual hierarchy = faster scannability & message retention

  ![Slite landing page before & after optimization](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Slite_large.webp "Slite landing page before & after optimization")**  

Image sources: [web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20220903073710/https://slite.com/compare/alternative-to-notion)
; [slite.com](https://slite.com/compare/alternative-to-notion)

**#### What changed

*   The 2022 version had large monochrome content blocks and minimal icons
    
*   The 2025 version uses color-coded benefit sections (pink, orange, black, white), modular cards with icons and headings, and more visual metaphors (clutter, remote work, ease of use)
    

#### Impact

*   The cleaner layout and stronger cues make it easier for users to scan, read, and retain the essentials
    
*   It also adds rhythm and variation across scroll depth
    

#### What you can learn

*   Make sure each section pops with purpose, but still flows as part of a connected journey
    
*   Use color blocking, iconography, and clear headlines to anchor attention
    

### Charlie HR: Personalization through team presence = higher trust

  ![Charlie HR landing page before & after optimization](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Charlie%20HR_block.webp "Charlie HR landing page before & after optimization")**  

Image sources: [web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20231201193925/https://www.charliehr.com/demo)
; [charliehr.com](https://www.charliehr.com/demo)

#### [](https://www.charliehr.com/demo)

**

#### What changed

*   In 2023, the page featured only one rep, Josh Hardy
    
*   The 2025 page adds Gabbi Montague-Smith, doubling the perceived support capacity and adding gender diversity to the team representation
    

#### Impact

*   Even subtle humanization like this boosts confidence and removes the “faceless SaaS” feel
    
*   It says “real people, real help”
    

#### What you can learn

*   Put faces to your funnel
    
*   People book demos with people, not logos, so if your reps are part of the experience, show them
    

Landing page optimization best practices
----------------------------------------

  

Conversion is a science. And every test you run sharpens the formula. Here’s how to start experiments that move the needle.

### 1\. Understand your audience’s intent

  

People click for a reason. Your job is to figure out which one: are they comparing options, ready to buy, or just browsing?  
  

You can use tools like Google Search Console (for query data), Hotjar polls, or Posthog event flows to see what brought them there.

  ![SME quote on landing page optimization](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Quote-2_block.webp "SME quote on landing page optimization")

👨‍💻 **Savvy move:** Add an exit-intent survey that asks, “What were you hoping to find here?”

  


****

### 2\. Focus on one goal per page

  

If your page is pulling in five directions, no one’s going to follow. Choose one goal: email sign-up, demo booking, or download, then cut everything else.

  

Use a single CTA style throughout and ditch unrelated links or navigation bars.

  

👨‍💻 **Savvy move:** Ask yourself, “If a user did just one thing on this page, what should it be?” Then make it unavoidable.

  


****

### 3\. Track conversions using event-based analytics

  

Page views tell you nothing about why people convert (or don’t). Event-based tracking lets you follow specific actions: form completions, scroll %, or button clicks.

  

Use tools like Plausible, Posthog, or Google Tag Manager to map these events.

  

👨‍💻 **Savvy move:** Track form field drop-off. You’ll quickly see if one field is scaring leads away.

  


****

### 4\. Don’t forget accessibility (color contrast, readable fonts, ARIA labels)

  

If your page only works for users with perfect vision, hearing, and reflexes, you exclude customers and tank conversions.  
  

Use tools like Stark (Figma plugin) or Wave to audit contrast, font size, ARIA tags, and keyboard navigation.  
  

👨‍💻 **Savvy move:** Test your page with no mouse and a screen reader. If you can’t complete the flow, fix it.

  


****

### 5\. Run continuous A/B testing (not one-and-done)

  

One test won’t save your funnel, since what works today might flop next week.

  

Optimization is a moving target. Start with high-impact areas like headlines, CTA copy, and form length. Use platforms like VWO, Google Optimize (sunsetting soon), or Convert.

  

👨‍💻 **Savvy move:** Run a rolling test schedule. Every month, test one big element and two micro tweaks.

  


****

### 6\. Use data to iterate, not guesswork

  

Your instincts can help, but data should make the final call.

  

Use quantitative tools (like analytics) and qualitative ones (like session replays or heatmaps). Check your bounce rate, time on page, and scroll depth together, not in isolation.

  

👨‍💻 **Savvy move:** Spot where 70%+ of users drop off and insert a CTA, testimonial, or visual anchor just above that spot.

  


****

==========================================================================

Dragos Voicila Content marketing manager

22 July 2025

Learn proven landing page optimization strategies to boost conversions, reduce bounce rates, and maximize ROI for your marketing campaigns.

**

Landing pages serve as the decisive moment in your marketing funnel, converting visitor intent into concrete actions like sign-ups, purchases, or inquiries. Through effective landing page optimization, you can achieve a higher click-through rate (CTR), better-quality leads, and stronger conversion rates without extra ad spend.

Read on if you’re looking for a straightforward blueprint to boost conversions.

What is the meaning of landing page optimization?
-------------------------------------------------

In doing so, you transform every interaction into a meaningful nudge toward your goal.  
  

So, whatever your goal — leads, conversions, or sales — optimization pushes it further. When every pixel pulls its weight, your page goes from performing to converting.

### Landing page optimization vs. website optimization

  

Here's how landing page optimization differs from website optimization.  
  


**

**Landing page optimization** revolves around one goal (like sign-ups or sales), making every element serve that single purpose. It’s campaign-specific, distraction-free, and built to convert fast. **Website optimization** supports a wider range of goals, from brand storytelling to SEO and user navigation. It’s about improving the full experience across multiple pages and audiences.

**

****  

Landing page visitors are primed to act, so [**landing page design**](https://www.edicy.com/blog/landing-page-design-for-higher-conversions)
 **optimization**

****

should guide, not distract. **Website optimization** should better help users explore, compare, and learn, requiring intuitive navigation and layered content.

****  

💡 In other words, landing pages drive immediate action while websites build long-term trust and discovery. Optimizing each for its role means better results across the entire [customer journey](https://www.textmagic.com/blog/b2b-customer-journey-map/)
.  

  ![Differences between landing page optimization and websit optimization](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Differences%20between%20landing%20page%20optimization%20and%20website%20optimization_block.webp "Differences between landing page optimization and websit optimization")

20 actionable landing page optimization tips
--------------------------------------------

  

Want more conversions from your landing pages? These 20 actionable tips will help you boost performance, reduce bounce rates, and turn more clicks into customers.

### How to optimize a landing page for lead generation

  

Your landing page should make it ridiculously easy for visitors to say “yes.” These tips help you capture high-quality leads without friction.

#### 1\. Use clear, compelling headlines that instantly show what’s in it for them

  

People scan before they read. If your headline doesn’t hook them in under 5 seconds, they’re gone.  
  

Therefore, lead with the payoff. For example, “Get 3x More Bookings Without Doubling Ad Spend.” Use direct language that reflects your ad or offer.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t use headlines like “Welcome” or “Let’s Get Started.” Those say nothing and sell nothing.

  


****

#### 2\. Keep forms short and ridiculously easy to complete

  ![Keeping forms short as a landing page optimization technique](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Screenshot%202025-07-22%20at%2013.18.06%201_block.webp "Keeping forms short as a landing page optimization technique")

Every extra field is a reason to bounce. Users aren’t here for paperwork; they’re here for value.

  

So, stick to the essentials: name + email. Want more info? Use progressive profiling or multi-step forms.

  

👍**Pro tip:** Label your submit button with the benefit, not the action. For example, “Get the Free Guide” > “Submit.”

  


****

#### 3\. Offer a strong lead magnet they’d actually trade their email for

  ![Offering a strong lead magnet as a landing page optimization technique](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/salesforce%2027_block.webp "Offering a strong lead magnet as a landing page optimization technique")

Image source: [salesforce.com](https://www.salesforce.com/eu/form/newsletter/?d=pb)

  

People don’t hand over personal info without a clear win. You need to give before you ask.  
  

Offer something bite-sized and instantly useful, like a checklist, a cheat sheet, or a free audit. Bonus if it solves a nagging problem.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t call it a “newsletter.” Nobody wakes up excited to subscribe to more emails.

  


****#### 4\. Use social proof to silence hesitation and build instant trust

  ![Using social proof as a landing page optimization technique](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Screenshot%202025-07-22%20at%2013.19.37%201_block.webp "Using social proof as a landing page optimization technique")**  

Image source: [textmagic.com](https://www.textmagic.com/)

[](https://www.salesforce.com/eu/form/newsletter/?d=pb)
**

We look to others before we act, especially online. Validation reduces risk.

If possible, add a client logo bar, a brief testimonial, or a user count (“Trusted by 12,000+ marketers”) near your CTA.  
  

👍 **Pro tip:** Use faces when you can. Testimonials with photos increase trust dramatically.

  


****

#### 5\. Design like a minimalist with a conversion goal

  

Visual clutter leads to cognitive overload and decision paralysis. A clean design guides action.  
  

Think of it this way: one column, one CTA, ample white space. Remove anything that doesn’t move users closer to your goal.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t bury your CTA in a sea of competing elements. If it’s hard to find, it won’t get clicked.

  


****

### Landing page SEO optimization tips

  

Search engines can bring you qualified traffic for free, but only if you play by their rules and keep users happy. Here’s how to optimize for both robots and real people.

#### 6\. Use a keyword-rich H1 that tells both Google and visitors what you’re about

  

Your H1 is prime real estate. It signals relevance to search engines and sets expectations for readers.  
  

Drop your primary keyword into a benefits-focused headline. For example, “Get Affordable Team Messaging with Text Automation.”  
  

👍 **Pro tip:** Don’t force it. If the keyword makes the headline awkward, Google (and humans) will notice.

  


****

#### 7\. Add title tags and meta descriptions that act like your ad in search results

  ![Adding title tags and meta descriptions as landing page optimization techniques](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Screenshot%202025-07-21%20at%2014.40.26%20copy_large.webp "Adding title tags and meta descriptions as landing page optimization techniques")

Your meta title is the headline of your search result, so you’d better make it count. Treat it like your 160-character elevator pitch.  
  

Keep title tags under 60 characters, and make sure your meta description includes a hook and a CTA. Think: “Automate your texts. Boost response rates. Start free.”  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t stuff keywords or write like a bot. Write like someone whose work is worth clicking on.

  


****

#### 8\. Use alt text for images to boost crawlability

  ![Using alt text as a landing page optimization technique](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Screenshot%202025-07-21%20at%2014.42.27%20copy_block.webp "Using alt text as a landing page optimization technique")

Search engines can’t see images, but they can read descriptions. And users with screen readers rely on them.  
  

So, describe what the image shows in clear, specific terms. For example, “Dashboard showing SMS campaign metrics” > “Chart.”  
  

👍 **Pro tip:** Use your keyword where relevant, but only if it makes sense in context.

  


****

#### 9\. Optimize for lightning-fast load times

  

Google prioritizes pages that load fast. Your users do too, especially if they’re on the go.  
  

Use tools like PageSpeed Insights. Compress images, ditch heavy scripts, and make sure your layout doesn’t break on small screens.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t rely on desktop previews. Test it on your phone, then test it again.

  


****

#### 10\. Add internal links (sparingly) to support your site’s SEO structure

  

Internal links help Google crawl your site and help users keep exploring.  
  

So, use descriptive anchor text to link to relevant resources like blog posts or pricing pages. For example: “See our pricing breakdown” > “Click here.”  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t overdo it. Too many links can feel spammy and kill your conversion focus.

  


****

### Design & UX tips for higher engagement

  

Every design choice is a cue for user behavior. These tips help you create landing pages that feel intuitive, load fast, and keep people scrolling (and converting).  

#### 11\. Use visual hierarchy and whitespace to guide the eye like a pro

  ![Using whitespace as a landing page optimization technique](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/19.%20Voog_block.webp "Using whitespace as a landing page optimization technique")

If your message isn’t skimmable, it’s skippable. A good hierarchy tells them where to look next without thinking.  
  

Make headlines bigger, CTAs bolder, and supporting copy lighter. Leave breathing room between sections so the page doesn’t feel like a wall of noise.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t cram everything above the fold. Let your content breathe. Scroll is free real estate.

  


****

#### 12\. Make sure your design is fully responsive, because desktop is not the default

  

More than [60%](https://whatsthebigdata.com/mobile-internet-traffic/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
 of traffic is mobile. If your layout breaks on a phone, your conversions will too.  
  

Use flexible grids, large tappable buttons, and font sizes that scale. Preview on multiple devices before launch.  
  

👍 **Pro tip:** Test thumb zones. If users have to pinch and zoom, you’ve already lost them.

  


****

#### 13\. Use high-contrast CTA buttons that beg to be clicked

  ![Using high-contrast CTAs as a landing page optimization technique](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/5.%20Mailchimp_block.webp "Using high-contrast CTAs as a landing page optimization technique")

Image source: [mailchimp.com](https://mailchimp.com/landers/email-marketing-platform/?ds_c=DEPT_AOC_Google_Search_ROW_EN_Brand_Acquire_Omega_Manual-NE_T3&ds_kids=p81005570474&ds_a_lid=kwd-2285511033&ds_cid=71700000120288589&ds_agid=58700008803527157&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=21865451006&gbraid=0AAAAADh1Fp3rRfLiP6ygRh8C0w8G4A13A&gclid=CjwKCAjw24vBBhABEiwANFG7y7OX8nLtcHrgBKFPnlc0MJiaSi5qOZrzcoxWpG_mtwLkPAk_XDQL7RoCKRYQAvD_BwE&gclsrc=aw.ds&currency=EUR)

[](https://mailchimp.com/landers/email-marketing-platform/?ds_c=DEPT_AOC_Google_Search_ROW_EN_Brand_Acquire_Omega_Manual-NE_T3&ds_kids=p81005570474&ds_a_lid=kwd-2285511033&ds_cid=71700000120288589&ds_agid=58700008803527157&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=21865451006&gbraid=0AAAAADh1Fp3rRfLiP6ygRh8C0w8G4A13A&gclid=CjwKCAjw24vBBhABEiwANFG7y7OX8nLtcHrgBKFPnlc0MJiaSi5qOZrzcoxWpG_mtwLkPAk_XDQL7RoCKRYQAvD_BwE&gclsrc=aw.ds&currency=EUR)
  

CTAs should be obvious. If visitors have to hunt for them, they won’t bother.  
  

Therefore, choose a button color that pops against your background. Think blue on white, orange on navy, not subtle greys.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t bury your CTA in a sea of text, nor match it to your background. You’re hunting conversions, not chameleons.

  


****

#### 14\. Add explainer videos or subtle animations to clarify, not distract

  

Viewers retain [95%](https://speach.me/blog/7-stats-that-prove-why-video-instructions-are-more-effective-than-written?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
 of a video's message compared to 10% when reading text. That is, if it’s used with purpose.  
  

Use short (<60 sec) videos to walk users through a process or show off product features. Keep animations smooth and sparing, with no flashing banners or spinning logos.  
  

👍 **Pro tip:** Always include captions. Many users watch on mute.

  


****#### 15\. Use scroll behavior analytics to find (and fix) dead zones

  ![Using heatmaps as a landing page optimization technique](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Hotjar-711x1024.png "Using heatmaps as a landing page optimization technique")**  

Image source: [textmagic.com](https://www.textmagic.com/blog/customer-engagement-metrics/)

**

You can’t optimize what you can’t see. Scroll maps reveal where users lose interest.  
  

Tools like Hotjar or Clarity show where visitors stop reading, rage-click, or scroll past your CTA. Adjust the layout accordingly.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t assume everyone reads top to bottom. Some of your best content might be invisible without data.

  


****

### How to improve landing page conversion rate

  

Getting clicks only means you’re visible. Our goal is to get you from “visible” to “valuable”, and that translates into conversions. The following tips help turn “maybe later” into “take my money.”

#### 16\. Run A/B tests like your ROI depends on it — because it does

  ![Running A/B tests as a landing page optimization technique](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/CTA_block.webp "Running A/B tests as a landing page optimization technique")

What you like doesn’t matter. What converts does.  
  

Start with big-impact variables: headline, CTA, offer. Test one element at a time and give it enough traffic to reach statistical confidence.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t call a test too early. Let the data breathe before making changes.

  


****#### 17\. Write CTA buttons that punch above their weight

  ![Writing punchy CTAs as a landing page optimization technique](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/7.%20Jolie_block.webp "Writing punchy CTAs as a landing page optimization technique")**  

Image source: [jolieskinco.com](https://jolieskinco.com/pages/water-report)

**

“Submit” is a shrug. A strong CTA makes the action irresistible.  
  

Use first-person, action-focused phrases tied to value. For example, “Start My Free Trial,” “Send Me the Tips,” “Book My Demo.”  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Avoid vague or passive language like “Learn More” or “Click Here”. Those say nothing and convert even less.

  


****

#### 18\. Strip out distractions like nav bars, footers, and links to nowhere

  

Every extra option is a chance to not convert. Fewer exits = more completions.  
  

Use a clean, single-purpose layout. Ditch global nav, sidebars, and any links that don’t push toward your goal.  
  

👍 **Pro tip:**  If you're worried about SEO or user needs, add collapsible sections or microcopy. Just don’t overload the page visually.

  


****

#### 19\. Mirror your ad copy to keep the message consistent from click to CTA

  

If the landing page doesn’t reflect the ad they clicked, visitors get disoriented. Or worse, annoyed.  
  

Reuse key phrases, offers, and tone from your ad in the headline and hero section. Maintain the emotional thread.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t promise a free guide in the ad and deliver a demo form. That’s a bait-and-bounce move.

  


****

#### 20\. Add urgency that’s honest, not gimmicky

  

Deadlines move people. Without one, “later” becomes “never.”  
  

Use countdown timers, such as “Only X Spots Left,” or phrases like “Offer Ends Sunday.” But make sure the timer is real.  
  

❌ **Mistake to avoid:** Don’t overdo it. Scarcity works best when it’s grounded in truth. If everything’s “limited-time,” nothing is.

****Three real-world landing page optimization examples
---------------------------------------------------

  

Want to see what great landing page optimization looks like in action? Here are three real-world examples that turned clicks into conversions.

### Flare: Trust signals elevated = increased credibility & scroll retention

  ![Flare landing page before & after optimization](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Flare_block.webp "Flare landing page before & after optimization")

Image sources: [web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20240610083653/https://try.flare.io/book-a-demo/)
; [try.flare.io](https://try.flare.io/book-a-demo/)

#### What changed

*   Strong offer in 2024 (“14-day full access”), but the absence of any trust cues above the fold made the value proposition feel unanchored
    
*   In the 2025 version, Flare introduces a “Verizon Business Contributor” badge right under the offer
    

#### Impact

*   A high-trust brand marker (e.g., Verizon) near the headline instantly boosts perceived legitimacy, especially among enterprise or compliance-driven decision-makers
    
*   It also visually breaks up the hero without clutter
    

#### What you can learn

*   A well-placed trust badge can outperform paragraphs of copy
    
*   Use recognizable brand associations above the fold to build instant authority
    

### Slite: Reworked visual hierarchy = faster scannability & message retention

  ![Slite landing page before & after optimization](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Slite_large.webp "Slite landing page before & after optimization")**  

Image sources: [web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20220903073710/https://slite.com/compare/alternative-to-notion)
; [slite.com](https://slite.com/compare/alternative-to-notion)

**#### What changed

*   The 2022 version had large monochrome content blocks and minimal icons
    
*   The 2025 version uses color-coded benefit sections (pink, orange, black, white), modular cards with icons and headings, and more visual metaphors (clutter, remote work, ease of use)
    

#### Impact

*   The cleaner layout and stronger cues make it easier for users to scan, read, and retain the essentials
    
*   It also adds rhythm and variation across scroll depth
    

#### What you can learn

*   Make sure each section pops with purpose, but still flows as part of a connected journey
    
*   Use color blocking, iconography, and clear headlines to anchor attention
    

### Charlie HR: Personalization through team presence = higher trust

  ![Charlie HR landing page before & after optimization](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Charlie%20HR_block.webp "Charlie HR landing page before & after optimization")**  

Image sources: [web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20231201193925/https://www.charliehr.com/demo)
; [charliehr.com](https://www.charliehr.com/demo)

#### [](https://www.charliehr.com/demo)

**

#### What changed

*   In 2023, the page featured only one rep, Josh Hardy
    
*   The 2025 page adds Gabbi Montague-Smith, doubling the perceived support capacity and adding gender diversity to the team representation
    

#### Impact

*   Even subtle humanization like this boosts confidence and removes the “faceless SaaS” feel
    
*   It says “real people, real help”
    

#### What you can learn

*   Put faces to your funnel
    
*   People book demos with people, not logos, so if your reps are part of the experience, show them
    

Landing page optimization best practices
----------------------------------------

  

Conversion is a science. And every test you run sharpens the formula. Here’s how to start experiments that move the needle.

### 1\. Understand your audience’s intent

  

People click for a reason. Your job is to figure out which one: are they comparing options, ready to buy, or just browsing?  
  

You can use tools like Google Search Console (for query data), Hotjar polls, or Posthog event flows to see what brought them there.

  ![SME quote on landing page optimization](https://media.voog.com/0000/0052/3783/photos/Quote-2_block.webp "SME quote on landing page optimization")

👨‍💻 **Savvy move:** Add an exit-intent survey that asks, “What were you hoping to find here?”

  


****

### 2\. Focus on one goal per page

  

If your page is pulling in five directions, no one’s going to follow. Choose one goal: email sign-up, demo booking, or download, then cut everything else.

  

Use a single CTA style throughout and ditch unrelated links or navigation bars.

  

👨‍💻 **Savvy move:** Ask yourself, “If a user did just one thing on this page, what should it be?” Then make it unavoidable.

  


****

### 3\. Track conversions using event-based analytics

  

Page views tell you nothing about why people convert (or don’t). Event-based tracking lets you follow specific actions: form completions, scroll %, or button clicks.

  

Use tools like Plausible, Posthog, or Google Tag Manager to map these events.

  

👨‍💻 **Savvy move:** Track form field drop-off. You’ll quickly see if one field is scaring leads away.

  


****

### 4\. Don’t forget accessibility (color contrast, readable fonts, ARIA labels)

  

If your page only works for users with perfect vision, hearing, and reflexes, you exclude customers and tank conversions.  
  

Use tools like Stark (Figma plugin) or Wave to audit contrast, font size, ARIA tags, and keyboard navigation.  
  

👨‍💻 **Savvy move:** Test your page with no mouse and a screen reader. If you can’t complete the flow, fix it.

  


****

### 5\. Run continuous A/B testing (not one-and-done)

  

One test won’t save your funnel, since what works today might flop next week.

  

Optimization is a moving target. Start with high-impact areas like headlines, CTA copy, and form length. Use platforms like VWO, Google Optimize (sunsetting soon), or Convert.

  

👨‍💻 **Savvy move:** Run a rolling test schedule. Every month, test one big element and two micro tweaks.

  


****

### 6\. Use data to iterate, not guesswork

  

Your instincts can help, but data should make the final call.

  

Use quantitative tools (like analytics) and qualitative ones (like session replays or heatmaps). Check your bounce rate, time on page, and scroll depth together, not in isolation.

  

👨‍💻 **Savvy move:** Spot where 70%+ of users drop off and insert a CTA, testimonial, or visual anchor just above that spot.

  


****

==============================================

Hello and welcome to another edition of my newsletter. My name is [Lenny](https://twitter.com/lennysan)
, and each week I tackle reader questions about product, growth, working with humans, and anything else that’s stressing you out at the office. [Send me your questions](https://forms.gle/JaTUeNAfRhAGCFn89)
 and in return, I’ll humbly offer actionable real-talk advice**. 🤝**

**If you find this newsletter valuable, consider [sharing it with friends](https://www.lennyrachitsky.com/)
 🤜🤛**

[Share](https://www.lennysnewsletter.com/p/this-week-21-strategy-and-tactics?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&action=share)

* * *

Q: A lot is written about driving traffic to a website, but not so much about how to convert that traffic into customers. Any best practices you can share? What had the most impact on conversion at Airbnb?


---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[![](https://www.lennysnewsletter.com/p/fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fbucketeer-e05bbc84-baa3-437e-9518-adb32be77984.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F8d39ff9d-86bc-4180-ab66-cf3ce250f2d1_480x270.gif)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!ukyA!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fbucketeer-e05bbc84-baa3-437e-9518-adb32be77984.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F8d39ff9d-86bc-4180-ab66-cf3ce250f2d1_480x270.gif)

**Increasing conversion (a.k.a fix the “leaks” in your funnel, get it?) is one of the highest ROI investments a growth team can make**, particularly once you’ve got your top-of-funnel growth engines (e.g. paid, SEO, referrals) up and running. Not only do conversion improvements make your existing growth channels more efficient, the wins last forever (…or at least until you decide to redesign everything).

When thinking about conversion, there are two places you can focus:

1.  **Keeping users** in the flow
    
2.  **Bringing users back** into the flow
    

Let’s go through these individually.

### **1\. Keeping users in the flow**

When I approach optimizing a funnel, I generally focus on three levers:

1.  **Maintain user focus** as they move through your flow 🧐
    
2.  **Maintain user motivation** as they move through your flow 🤗
    
3.  **Reduce user friction** so that they can easily move through your flow 😄
    

You and your team can leverage the above framework by [coming up with ideas](https://www.lennyrachitsky.com/p/where-great-product-roadmap-ideas)
 within each of these three levers, and then testing out your favorites. My advice is to experiment with as many ideas as you can, vs. betting on just a few amazing ideas.

If running experiments isn’t possible at your scale (you can use [this handy calculator](https://www.optimizely.com/sample-size-calculator/)
 to get a sense), my advice is to do your due diligence (e.g. talk to users, evaluation upside, etc.), but then feel comfortable trusting yourself to go with your best guesses.

Airbnb has an incredibly strong culture of [experimentation](https://medium.com/airbnb-engineering/experiment-reporting-framework-4e3fcd29e6c0)
 and [iteration](https://medium.com/airbnb-engineering/4-principles-for-making-experimentation-count-7a5f1a5268a)
, and the volume to support it. By the time I left, we had hundreds of experiments running at any given time. From that experimentation, here are some of the biggest conversion wins at Airbnb, that I’m familiar with (by lever):

**Lever 1: Maintain user focus** 🧐

1.  **Opening listings in a new tab**: When you click on an Airbnb listing (in search, from the home page, etc.), it always opens up in a new tab. Why? We found that helping a user avoid losing track of all of their options helps them continue exploring, especially if that first listing didn’t work out. This turned out to be one of the biggest conversion wins 🤷‍♂️
    
2.  **Neighborhoods:** In late 2012, Airbnb [launched a product called “Neighborhoods”](https://techcrunch.com/2012/11/13/airbnb-launches-neighborhoods-providing-the-definitive-travel-guide-for-its-guests/)
     which offered users incredibly rich and unique content about individual neighborhoods around the world. Visitors loved it. Almost too much. It turned out the content was so interesting that it distracted visitors from actually booking. When the team removed it from the home page, bookings went up.
    
3.  **Setting dates**: When you search for a place to stay on Airbnb, you’re encouraged to input the dates for your trip. Though that introduces a tiny bit of friction, it turns out that by restricting your results to homes that are _actually_ available during your trip, you avoid distracting users with better but unavailable options. Adding this prompt had a big impact.
    

**Lever 2: Maintain user motivation** 🤗

1.  **Scarcity**: Giving users a reason to act now, by conveying a sense of [scarcity](https://www.influenceatwork.com/principles-of-persuasion/#scarcity)
     (e.g. this property is usually booked), is a powerful motivator and a big conversion opportunity.
    
2.  **Highlights**: Reminding users what’s great about the property they’re booking (e.g. the location, the amenities, the price) helps them avoid reconsidering and bailing, leading to great conversion wins.
    
3.  **What’s my place worth:** On the host side, the primary motivation for becoming a host is income. Thus, making this value-prop prominent not only on [the host landing page](https://www.airbnb.com/host/homes)
    , but also throughout the entire new-host-flow (and follow-up emails), was impactful.
    

**Lever 3: Reduce user friction** 😄

1.  **Instant Book**: By far the biggest friction to booking on Airbnb has always been the host approval process. Over the years, [as the platform shifted to predominantly Instant Book](https://www.phocuswire.com/Airbnb-instant-booking-growth)
    , guest conversion _significantly_ increased as a result.
    
2.  **Smart defaults**: When you can’t remove steps from a flow, the next best thing is to set smart default answers. For example, as a new host, listing your home involves dozens of questions — your availability, your price, your listing title. We found a lot of success in setting smart default answers (or recommended answers) to as many of these questions as possible, making it easy for new hosts to move through the flow efficiently.
    
3.  **Performance:** Slow page/app performance is one of the worst types of friction. It frustrates users, has nothing to do with your actual product, and is often invisible to your team. Though it won’t always work, and it’s often time-consuming to fix, we saw improvements in performance make a big dent in conversion, particularly on mobile.
    

No matter how great your flow is, users will bounce, so let’s talk about bringing them back.

### **2\. Bringing users back into the flow**

Most of your bounced users won’t actually want what you’re selling (sorry). But, a significant percentage of bounced users are just not ready to buy right then, or got distracted by another task, or got confused by your flow. This latter group of users is the users you want to target with a re-engagement strategy.

There are two key questions to consider when attempting to re-engage users:

1.  WHAT can you tell them to convince them to try again?
    
2.  HOW do you reach them?
    

**WHAT to tell bounced users**

The three core content strategies for re-engaging users (though there are probably more):

1.  **A reminder**: You tried to do this thing and you didn’t finish. Want to finish?
    
2.  **Something has changed**: Since the time you tried to book, prices have come down. Want to try again?
    
3.  **There’s more information**: Looks like you stopped at this step — did you know that it’s optional?
    

At Airbnb, we had the most success with:

1.  Reminding hosts a guest is waiting for a response
    
2.  Reminding visitors that a home they were looking at was still available
    
3.  Changes in market conditions (e.g. homes are getting booked)
    
4.  Changes to prices (e.g. this listing is now cheaper)
    
5.  Letting new hosts know they were only X steps away from becoming a host
    

Think about what value you can provide your users that would give them a good reason to try again.

**HOW to reach bounced users**

And finally, having a great message is one thing, but getting to your users is another. There are essentially only three re-engagement channels:

1.  **Emails/push notifications**: Simple, effective, but easy to abuse.
    
2.  **Retargeting**: Paid ads that target site visitors.
    
3.  **Calls:** Calling prospects that have dropped off.
    

At Airbnb, we employed all three, but mostly email and retargeting. Both were extremely effective, early-on and at scale.

**To go deeper, here are a few articles I recommend:**

1.  [A/B Testing](https://www.julian.com/guide/growth/ab-testing)
     by Julian Shapiro
    
2.  [Conversion Rate Optimization](https://moz.com/learn/seo/conversion-rate-optimization)
     by Moz
    
3.  [The Conversion Optimization Rulebook](https://unbounce.com/conversion-rate-optimization/rulebook/)
     by Unbounce
    
4.  [Psych’d: A new user psychology framework for increasing funnel conversion](https://andrewchen.co/psychd-funnel-conversion/)
     by Darius Contractor
    
5.  [13 Examples of Re-Engagement Emails](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/10-examples-of-effective-re-engagement-emails)
     by HubSpot
    

Now go fix those leaks.

Hello and welcome to another edition of my newsletter. My name is [Lenny](https://twitter.com/lennysan)
, and each week I tackle reader questions about product, growth, working with humans, and anything else that’s stressing you out at the office. [Send me your questions](https://forms.gle/JaTUeNAfRhAGCFn89)
 and in return, I’ll humbly offer actionable real-talk advice**. 🤝**

**If you find this newsletter valuable, consider [sharing it with friends](https://www.lennyrachitsky.com/)
 🤜🤛**

[Share](https://www.lennysnewsletter.com/p/this-week-21-strategy-and-tactics?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&action=share)

Q: A lot is written about driving traffic to a website, but not so much about how to convert that traffic into customers. Any best practices you can share? What had the most impact on conversion at Airbnb?


---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[![](https://www.lennysnewsletter.com/p/fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fbucketeer-e05bbc84-baa3-437e-9518-adb32be77984.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F8d39ff9d-86bc-4180-ab66-cf3ce250f2d1_480x270.gif)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!ukyA!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fbucketeer-e05bbc84-baa3-437e-9518-adb32be77984.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F8d39ff9d-86bc-4180-ab66-cf3ce250f2d1_480x270.gif)

**Increasing conversion (a.k.a fix the “leaks” in your funnel, get it?) is one of the highest ROI investments a growth team can make**, particularly once you’ve got your top-of-funnel growth engines (e.g. paid, SEO, referrals) up and running. Not only do conversion improvements make your existing growth channels more efficient, the wins last forever (…or at least until you decide to redesign everything).

When thinking about conversion, there are two places you can focus:

1.  **Keeping users** in the flow
    
2.  **Bringing users back** into the flow
    

Let’s go through these individually.

### **1\. Keeping users in the flow**

When I approach optimizing a funnel, I generally focus on three levers:

1.  **Maintain user focus** as they move through your flow 🧐
    
2.  **Maintain user motivation** as they move through your flow 🤗
    
3.  **Reduce user friction** so that they can easily move through your flow 😄
    

You and your team can leverage the above framework by [coming up with ideas](https://www.lennyrachitsky.com/p/where-great-product-roadmap-ideas)
 within each of these three levers, and then testing out your favorites. My advice is to experiment with as many ideas as you can, vs. betting on just a few amazing ideas.

If running experiments isn’t possible at your scale (you can use [this handy calculator](https://www.optimizely.com/sample-size-calculator/)
 to get a sense), my advice is to do your due diligence (e.g. talk to users, evaluation upside, etc.), but then feel comfortable trusting yourself to go with your best guesses.

Airbnb has an incredibly strong culture of [experimentation](https://medium.com/airbnb-engineering/experiment-reporting-framework-4e3fcd29e6c0)
 and [iteration](https://medium.com/airbnb-engineering/4-principles-for-making-experimentation-count-7a5f1a5268a)
, and the volume to support it. By the time I left, we had hundreds of experiments running at any given time. From that experimentation, here are some of the biggest conversion wins at Airbnb, that I’m familiar with (by lever):

**Lever 1: Maintain user focus** 🧐

1.  **Opening listings in a new tab**: When you click on an Airbnb listing (in search, from the home page, etc.), it always opens up in a new tab. Why? We found that helping a user avoid losing track of all of their options helps them continue exploring, especially if that first listing didn’t work out. This turned out to be one of the biggest conversion wins 🤷‍♂️
    
2.  **Neighborhoods:** In late 2012, Airbnb [launched a product called “Neighborhoods”](https://techcrunch.com/2012/11/13/airbnb-launches-neighborhoods-providing-the-definitive-travel-guide-for-its-guests/)
     which offered users incredibly rich and unique content about individual neighborhoods around the world. Visitors loved it. Almost too much. It turned out the content was so interesting that it distracted visitors from actually booking. When the team removed it from the home page, bookings went up.
    
3.  **Setting dates**: When you search for a place to stay on Airbnb, you’re encouraged to input the dates for your trip. Though that introduces a tiny bit of friction, it turns out that by restricting your results to homes that are _actually_ available during your trip, you avoid distracting users with better but unavailable options. Adding this prompt had a big impact.
    

**Lever 2: Maintain user motivation** 🤗

1.  **Scarcity**: Giving users a reason to act now, by conveying a sense of [scarcity](https://www.influenceatwork.com/principles-of-persuasion/#scarcity)
     (e.g. this property is usually booked), is a powerful motivator and a big conversion opportunity.
    
2.  **Highlights**: Reminding users what’s great about the property they’re booking (e.g. the location, the amenities, the price) helps them avoid reconsidering and bailing, leading to great conversion wins.
    
3.  **What’s my place worth:** On the host side, the primary motivation for becoming a host is income. Thus, making this value-prop prominent not only on [the host landing page](https://www.airbnb.com/host/homes)
    , but also throughout the entire new-host-flow (and follow-up emails), was impactful.
    

**Lever 3: Reduce user friction** 😄

1.  **Instant Book**: By far the biggest friction to booking on Airbnb has always been the host approval process. Over the years, [as the platform shifted to predominantly Instant Book](https://www.phocuswire.com/Airbnb-instant-booking-growth)
    , guest conversion _significantly_ increased as a result.
    
2.  **Smart defaults**: When you can’t remove steps from a flow, the next best thing is to set smart default answers. For example, as a new host, listing your home involves dozens of questions — your availability, your price, your listing title. We found a lot of success in setting smart default answers (or recommended answers) to as many of these questions as possible, making it easy for new hosts to move through the flow efficiently.
    
3.  **Performance:** Slow page/app performance is one of the worst types of friction. It frustrates users, has nothing to do with your actual product, and is often invisible to your team. Though it won’t always work, and it’s often time-consuming to fix, we saw improvements in performance make a big dent in conversion, particularly on mobile.
    

No matter how great your flow is, users will bounce, so let’s talk about bringing them back.

### **2\. Bringing users back into the flow**

Most of your bounced users won’t actually want what you’re selling (sorry). But, a significant percentage of bounced users are just not ready to buy right then, or got distracted by another task, or got confused by your flow. This latter group of users is the users you want to target with a re-engagement strategy.

There are two key questions to consider when attempting to re-engage users:

1.  WHAT can you tell them to convince them to try again?
    
2.  HOW do you reach them?
    

**WHAT to tell bounced users**

The three core content strategies for re-engaging users (though there are probably more):

1.  **A reminder**: You tried to do this thing and you didn’t finish. Want to finish?
    
2.  **Something has changed**: Since the time you tried to book, prices have come down. Want to try again?
    
3.  **There’s more information**: Looks like you stopped at this step — did you know that it’s optional?
    

At Airbnb, we had the most success with:

1.  Reminding hosts a guest is waiting for a response
    
2.  Reminding visitors that a home they were looking at was still available
    
3.  Changes in market conditions (e.g. homes are getting booked)
    
4.  Changes to prices (e.g. this listing is now cheaper)
    
5.  Letting new hosts know they were only X steps away from becoming a host
    

Think about what value you can provide your users that would give them a good reason to try again.

**HOW to reach bounced users**

And finally, having a great message is one thing, but getting to your users is another. There are essentially only three re-engagement channels:

1.  **Emails/push notifications**: Simple, effective, but easy to abuse.
    
2.  **Retargeting**: Paid ads that target site visitors.
    
3.  **Calls:** Calling prospects that have dropped off.
    

At Airbnb, we employed all three, but mostly email and retargeting. Both were extremely effective, early-on and at scale.

**To go deeper, here are a few articles I recommend:**

1.  [A/B Testing](https://www.julian.com/guide/growth/ab-testing)
     by Julian Shapiro
    
2.  [Conversion Rate Optimization](https://moz.com/learn/seo/conversion-rate-optimization)
     by Moz
    
3.  [The Conversion Optimization Rulebook](https://unbounce.com/conversion-rate-optimization/rulebook/)
     by Unbounce
    
4.  [Psych’d: A new user psychology framework for increasing funnel conversion](https://andrewchen.co/psychd-funnel-conversion/)
     by Darius Contractor
    
5.  [13 Examples of Re-Engagement Emails](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/10-examples-of-effective-re-engagement-emails)
     by HubSpot
    

Now go fix those leaks.

Landing Page Optimization: 12 Best Practices With Examples (2026)
=================================================================

![Author Waseem Bashir](https://www.apexure.com/images/author-wb.svg)

By [Waseem Bashir,](https://www.apexure.com/blog/landing-page-optimization-best-practices-with-examples#about_author)
 CEO

![updated-date-icon](https://www.apexure.com/images/updated-date-icon.svg)

Updated on 21 Mar, 2026

Key Takeaways
-------------

*   Landing page optimization is not a one-time project, it is an ongoing cycle of research, hypothesis building, testing, and iteration.
*   The five highest-impact optimisation areas: form length reduction (up to 120% lift), headline-ad message match, page speed, social proof placement, and single CTA focus.
*   53% of mobile users abandon pages that load in over 3 seconds. Mobile accounts for 83% of traffic but converts at roughly half the rate of desktop.
*   Every optimisation test should follow the EPIC framework: score by Experimentation, Priority, Impact, and Cost before committing resources.
*   These best practices come from 3,000+ landing page projects and 800+ A/B tests across 300+ clients at Apexure.

Optimising a landing page only after its conversion rate drops is a losing strategy. By that point you are already behind, dealing with an overwhelming pile of unsorted data, not enough time to test every hypothesis, and pressure from leadership to make gut-based decisions. Landing page optimization works best as a proactive, continuous process. You set up tracking, watch how users actually behave, build data-informed hypotheses, test them, and feed the results back into the next round. Done well, it compounds, each cycle makes the page better and teaches you something about your audience that your competitors do not know. After building and optimising 3,000+ landing pages across 300+ clients. We have distilled our process into 12 best practices that consistently produce measurable results. This guide walks you through each one with examples from our own work.

THE LANDING PAGE OPTIMIZATION CYCLE Not a one-time fix, a continuous process that compounds over time 1 Track Set KPIs Install tools Collect data → 2 Analyse Quant + qual data Heatmaps Session recordings → 3 Hypothesise Build test ideas Define success Link to data → 4 Prioritise EPIC framework Score each test Rank by ROI → 5 Test A/B experiments Stat significance Roll out winners → 6 Learn Document results Feed back to Step 1 Compound gains Each cycle teaches you something new. The best landing pages are never "done." Based on Apexure's EPIC framework | 800+ A/B tests across 300+ clients

What is landing page optimization?
----------------------------------

Landing page optimization (LPO) is the process of improving every element of a landing page, from headline copy to form design to page speed, using data-driven insights. The goal is to increase the percentage of visitors who complete the desired action, whether that is filling out a form, booking a demo, or making a purchase. As a business owner, understanding LPO matters because your landing pages are the conversion layer of your marketing. You can have the best ads in the world, but if the page they land on fails to convert, every click is wasted spend.

![author-image](https://www.apexure.com/uploads/waseem-bashir-ceo-apexure-0ae1db.webp)

Without optimized landing pages, you are wasting money, time, and opportunities on Google Ads. Conversion is the goal; if the page fails, so does the campaign.

\-[Waseem Bashir](https://www.apexure.com/blog/landing-page-optimization-best-practices-with-examples)
  Founder & CEO at Apexure

![tdesign_link_icon](https://www.apexure.com/images/tdesign_link_icon.svg)

[The Complete Guide to CRO ![link_arrow](https://www.apexure.com/images/link-to-source-arrow.svg)](https://www.apexure.com/blog/conversion-rate-optimisation-guide/)
 

12 landing page optimization best practices
-------------------------------------------

These are the practices that consistently produce results in our testing. They are ordered by where they fit in the optimisation cycle, from setting up measurement to running tests to building feedback loops.

### 1\. Define your KPIs before touching anything

Before changing a single element, decide what you are measuring and why. Most teams track conversion rate and nothing else. That is not enough. The KPIs that actually tell you where to focus:

*   **Conversion rate**, the obvious one, but segment it by traffic source, device, and campaign
*   **Form start rate**, what percentage of visitors begin filling out the form?
*   **Form completion rate**, of those who start, how many finish?
*   **Bounce rate**, are visitors leaving immediately? If so, message match is likely the problem
*   **Average engagement time**, how long are visitors actually spending on the page?
*   **Scroll depth**, are visitors reaching your CTA, or dropping off before they see it? GA4 tracks all of these. Set them up before your page goes live, not after something breaks.

![tdesign_link_icon](https://www.apexure.com/images/tdesign_link_icon.svg)

### 2\. Start tracking at the right time

When and how often you review data depends on traffic volume:

*   Review daily. You have enough data to spot trends quickly and catch problems before they cost you significant conversions.
*   Review weekly. Daily fluctuations will be noise. Focus on weekly patterns and give A/B tests longer to reach significance.

![author-image](https://www.apexure.com/uploads/waseem-bashir-ceo-apexure-0ae1db.webp)

Review landing pages every two weeks — or weekly for high-traffic sites. Benchmark against industry standards and adjust based on A/B test results.

### 3\. Build your optimisation toolkit

Metrics tell part of the story. To understand WHY visitors behave the way they do, you need UX research tools alongside analytics.

#### Quantitative Tools (What)

*   GA4, traffic, funnels, conversion tracking
*   Google PageSpeed Insights, Core Web Vitals
*   Looker Studio, custom dashboards
*   Search Console, query performance

#### Qualitative Tools (Why)

*   Hotjar / Clarity, heatmaps, session recordings
*   VWO / Optimizely, A/B testing platform
*   Wynter / UserTesting, user feedback
*   Maze, unmoderated usability tests

You do not need every tool on day one. Start with GA4 and one heatmap tool (Hotjar or Microsoft Clarity, both have free tiers). Add A/B testing when you have enough traffic to run statistically valid experiments.

### 4\. Combine quantitative and qualitative data

This is where most optimisation efforts stall. Teams look at GA4, see a high bounce rate, and immediately start redesigning the hero section. But bounce rate alone does not tell you WHY visitors leave.

**Quantitative data** (GA4, funnel reports) shows you WHAT is happening: page views, drop-off points, conversion rates.

**Qualitative data** (heatmaps, session recordings, surveys) shows you WHY: where users click, how far they scroll, what confuses them. Together. They give you hypotheses worth testing. A high bounce rate plus a heatmap showing rage clicks on a non-clickable hero image tells you something specific and actionable. A high bounce rate alone tells you almost nothing.

**Watch 20 session recordings before forming any hypothesis.** We do this on every new client engagement at Apexure. It takes 90 minutes and consistently reveals problems that no dashboard would surface, broken form fields on specific browsers, confusing navigation patterns, users trying to click on elements that are not clickable.

![tdesign_link_icon](https://www.apexure.com/images/tdesign_link_icon.svg)

[How To Do Landing Page Analysis The Right Way ![link_arrow](https://www.apexure.com/images/link-to-source-arrow.svg)](https://www.apexure.com/blog/landing-page-analysis-the-right-way)
 

### 5\. Build testable hypotheses

A hypothesis is not “let us try a different button colour.” A hypothesis has three parts: action, outcome, and reasoning.

**Template:** “If we \[action\], then \[outcome\] will improve, because \[reasoning based on data\].”

**Example:** “If we move the client logos from the footer to directly above the CTA button, then form submissions will increase, because heatmap data shows 60% of visitors never scroll past the fold and our highest-converting traffic source (Google Ads) has the lowest scroll depth.” Without the reasoning, you are guessing. With it, you are learning, even when the test loses, because a failed hypothesis tells you something about your audience.

![tdesign_link_icon](https://www.apexure.com/images/tdesign_link_icon.svg)

[Landing Page Testing Basics For Faster Optimization ![link_arrow](https://www.apexure.com/images/link-to-source-arrow.svg)](https://www.apexure.com/blog/landing-page-testing-basics-for-better-and-faster-optimization)
 

### 6\. Prioritise tests with the EPIC framework

After a thorough research phase, you will have 15-20 hypotheses. You can test maybe 3-4 per month. Choosing the wrong three means months of wasted capacity. At Apexure, we score every hypothesis using the [EPIC framework](https://www.apexure.com/blog/hire-a-cro-consultant)
:

THE EPIC CRO FRAMEWORK Score each hypothesis 1-5 on four dimensions. Highest total score runs first. E Experimentation 1 = safe incremental 5 = bold new approach P Priority 1 = nice-to-have 5 = revenue blocker I Impact 1 = marginal gain 5 = major C Cost 1 = weeks of dev work 5 = quick to implement A simple copy change scoring 17/20 should be tested before a complex redesign scoring 14/20.

This prevents the most common optimisation trap: testing whatever is easiest or whatever the CEO mentioned in the last meeting. We have seen teams spend three months A/B testing hero images when the real conversion killer was a five-field form that could have been two fields.

### 7\. Build a feedback loop

Every test, win, lose, or inconclusive, teaches you something about your users. The teams that compound their conversion gains are the ones that document and apply these learnings. After each test cycle:

1.  Record what you tested, why, and the result
2.  Update your hypothesis backlog based on what you learned
3.  Identify patterns across multiple tests (e.g., “trust signals consistently outperform urgency tactics for this audience”)
4.  Feed insights back into the next round of research This creates a knowledge base that makes each subsequent round of optimisation more efficient and more likely to produce winners.

Landing page optimization checklist

These are the tactical elements to audit and test on any landing page. We have organised them by category so you can focus on your weakest area first.

### Functionality

#### Page speed

[53% of mobile users abandon pages](https://www.thinkwithgoogle.com/marketing-strategies/app-and-mobile/page-load-time-statistics/)
 that take over 3 seconds to load. In 2026, Google’s Core Web Vitals set clear thresholds:

<2.5s LCP targetLargest Contentful Paint

<200ms INP targetInteraction to Next Paint

<0.1 CLS targetCumulative Layout Shift

Use Google PageSpeed Insights to check your scores. Focus on LCP first, it has the biggest impact on both bounce rate and [Google Ads Quality Score](https://www.apexure.com/blog/pagespeed-and-load-time-insights-for-websites-and-landingpages)
.

#### Layout and visual hierarchy

Experiment with layouts that maintain clear visual hierarchy and effective use of whitespace. Your page should guide the eye from headline to value proposition to social proof to CTA in a natural flow. Session recordings are invaluable here. They show you exactly how visitors move through your page, revealing confusing navigation paths and missed elements that analytics alone cannot surface.

#### Continuous testing

Do not treat optimisation as a one-off project. Regular A/B testing protects your conversion rate against audience shifts, competitor changes, and seasonal variations. Set up a testing calendar and commit to running at least 2-3 tests per month.

### Mobile responsiveness

83% of traffic now comes from mobile, but mobile converts at roughly half the rate of desktop (2.9% vs 5.1% on average). Closing that gap is one of the highest-ROI optimisation opportunities.

#### Common Mobile UX Problems

*   Buttons too small for thumb tapping
*   Text requires pinching to read
*   Forms with tiny input fields
*   Desktop layout squeezed onto mobile
*   CTAs below the fold on mobile screens

#### Mobile-First Fixes

*   Minimum 48px touch targets (WCAG standard)
*   16px+ body text for readability
*   Full-width form fields with proper keyboard types
*   Single-column layout with stacked sections
*   Sticky CTA bar at bottom of screen

![author-image](https://www.apexure.com/uploads/waseem-bashir-ceo-apexure-0ae1db.webp)

Mobile optimization is often neglected. Mobile users need tailored experiences with larger buttons, readable text, and device-specific designs — especially for older demographics.
